title: Muru
summary_raw: Muru Graham Dumpleton started mod_wsgi 20 years ago, and has been thinking about the ideal way to serve Python web applications in production ever since. Muru is his new, AI-assisted Rust server that aims to provide the best possible tools for running ASGI and WSGI Python apps both in development and production. As he did with wrapture , he's been publishing an extraordinarily detailed account of the project as he works on it - as part of his development process. Here's everything he's published so far, all in the last three weeks: 2026-11-04 — Twenty years of mod_wsgi, and what comes next 202

title: Nvidia researchers argue huge AI context windows are a dead end
summary_raw: Nvidia researchers argue that language models often don't need their full context windows—which are slow, expensive, and prone to errors—and propose an alternative. In tests, periodic summaries and targeted keyword search usually matched full-context results at a fraction of the cost. The team even proposes a new class of models that works with short notes instead of long context. title: Silicon Valley's growing obsession with AI doomsday is turning parts of the tech industry toward cult-like devotion
summary_raw: A Buddhist monastery in Vermont called Maple wants to establish itself as Silicon Valley's spiritual authority while creating its own AI god. According to a New Yorker report, leader Soryu Forall's group records every breath its members take to train an AI in his image. Former members report manipulation and psychological breakdowns. title: OpenAI shares new prompting tips for GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol to fix brief answers and unnecessary questions
summary_raw: OpenAI has released new prompt templates for GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol meant to fix common model behaviors such as overly brief answers, unnecessary follow-up questions, and excessive testing when coding. The API is changing as well, since editing a conversation's history can discard reasoning content and lower response quality. title: Hours after Anthropic claims a Claude proof of the Riemann hypothesis, Stanford releases an all-human competing draft
summary_raw: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says he used Claude to prove the Riemann hypothesis, math's most famous open problem for 167 years, with a proof formalized in Lean that spans over 250,000 pages. Just hours later, Stanford researchers published an independent, entirely human competing proof, and mathematicians are now checking whether either one holds up. title: New open model Inkling 2 Mini thinks in loops to solve problems with fewer words and still runs on a laptop
summary_raw: Thinking Machines has released Inkling 2 Mini, an open looped transformer that runs 12 of its 24 layers three times per token. This lets the model reason internally for longer without generating extra text. On Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index, it ties with Qwen3.8 27B at roughly six times lower cost. title: US technology stocks suffer their worst weekly loss since the pandemic as AI doubts pile up
summary_raw: The Nasdaq 100 has slipped into a bear market after its worst weekly loss since the Covid-19 crisis. Nvidia plunged 14 percent as the SEC reviews its accounting, and Anthropic lost nearly all of its gains a day after its record IPO. AI doubts, scandals, rising interest rates, and political headwinds are hitting overheated valuations all at once. title: Bytedance argues most AI training phases are unnecessary and backs it up with a competitive open model
summary_raw: Bytedance and several US universities introduce Axion 1.0, an AI agent that rivals top commercial models from OpenAI and Anthropic on benchmarks after just three training phases. The researchers attribute the gains to carefully curated training data rather than ever more training steps. The model, data, and code are freely available. summary_raw: TensorLean, from Columbia University and CertiK, formally verifies production GPU kernels at the PTX level using Lean.
